items.q: Amir's poem asks his lost love to come back in a dream. Does this line read as poetry?

items.text: 我绝不会以任何代价接受所罗门的那枚印戒
items.q: Amir reads a fragment of a Hafez poem. Does it read like classical poetry?

items.text: 是“阿塔尔哭到天明更觉甜美”那句，还是“如今他被杀得更彻底了”那句？
items.q: Two lines are quoted from a song set to Attar's poems. Do they sound like song lyrics?
before: ——好，就那首配着阿塔尔诗句的。

items.text: 我心里亮堂堂的：明天，当我睁开眼睛，一切都会结束，黑暗会再次回到我的梦中。
items.q: A poetic chapter ends its first passage this way. Does it read smoothly and poetically?

items.text: 缝的一边压着我多年信念中的种种界限与神圣性，沉甸甸的；缝的另一边，尼鲁法尔站着。
items.q: The narrator is torn between his old beliefs and a girl. Does this image read naturally?

items.text: 我还要说，我只有半小时。
items.q: A student answers Amir by email, short and cool. Does this sound natural?
before: – 这周我完全没有时间。下周四下午三点，上次我们见面的同一个地方。

items.text: 你得从你这个庇护所里走出来，真真切切去做点什么，而不是跑来这儿坐着空想。
items.q: Niloofar tells shy Amir to come out of his shell and act. Does this sound natural?
before: ——我知道，我又不傻。可这样不行。

items.text: 我爱您已经三十二个月了。从远处。不让您知道。
items.q: Shy Amir finally tells a fellow student he loves her, very formally. Does it sound natural?
before: 我走过去，在瓦利阿斯尔街这条人行道另一侧的那棵悬铃木下等着，等尼鲁法尔从其他人中抽身，好上前去当面告诉她：我爱她。

items.q: Niloofar playfully teases Amir for listening in on her. Does this sound natural?
before: ——今天在学院当中，你跟另外几个女生说话，我听见了。

items.text: 我脖子上哪儿写着“落脚处”呢？
items.q: Farid complains that Sajad stepped on his neck to climb into bed. Is this sarcastic complaint clear?
before: – 哎哟，哎哟。鹰眼，把你的脚从我脖子上挪开。
– 哎，对不起。客观地说，我是想回自己床上去。太难了。

items.text: 那就想想我们可怜的巴巴要受多大的罪——他这么多年都闲坐在家里。
items.q: Ghassem jokes, holding back a laugh, about his idle father. Does the irony come through?

items.text: 嗯，我们的巴巴·江可真是饿极了，饿的是尊重。
items.q: Ghassem jokes sarcastically that his father craves respect. Does this sound natural?

items.text: 可他偏偏找错了人；那点尊重被我们砸得一丝不剩。
items.q: Ghassem jokes that the family never gave his father any respect. Does this sound natural?
before: – 他可真是饿极了，饿的是尊重。

items.text: 我也要看。我没力气起来。
items.q: Hooman is too lazy to get up. Does this sound natural?
before: – 喂，豹子法里德，把那台笔记本拿过来，

items.text: 嘿，豹子法里德，给我，我占一卦。
items.q: Hooman wants the Hafez book to tell his fortune with it. Does '占一卦' fit here?

items.text: 豹子法里德，控制好你的脾气，别使出什么要命的招数。
items.q: Hooman's running joke is Farid's sudden 'murderous moves'. Does '要命的招数' work as a teasing phrase?
